questions.prompt: Which interface consideration becomes especially important when persistent mouth leak is limiting effective nasal PAP therapy?
options: Consider an oronasal or full-face option if appropriate
questions.answer: Consider an oronasal or full-face option if appropriate
questions.rationale: Persistent mouth leak may require a different interface approach when nasal PAP alone is not being tolerated effectively.

questions.prompt: Which PAP response is appropriate when hypopneas persist but snoring has resolved?
questions.rationale: Persistent obstructive hypopneas during PAP titration generally call for upward pressure adjustment rather than lowering pressure or adding oxygen first.

questions.prompt: Which situation most strongly raises concern for treatment-emergent central events during PAP titration?
options: Central apneas appear after obstructive events improve with pressure
questions.answer: Central apneas appear after obstructive events improve with pressure
questions.rationale: Central events that emerge as obstruction resolves with PAP raise concern for treatment-emergent central apnea.

questions.prompt: Which statement best fits positional therapy in obstructive sleep apnea care?
options: It aims to reduce events that worsen in certain body positions
It is only used during MSLT
It replaces all PAP treatment in every patient
It is a scoring method rather than a therapy
questions.answer: It aims to reduce events that worsen in certain body positions
questions.rationale: Positional therapy is directed at patients whose obstruction is significantly worse in specific sleep positions.

questions.prompt: Which statement best fits oral appliance therapy in sleep medicine?
options: It has no role outside pediatrics
It may be an alternative treatment option for selected obstructive cases
It is only for central apnea
questions.answer: It may be an alternative treatment option for selected obstructive cases
questions.rationale: Oral appliance therapy can be an alternative option in selected obstructive sleep apnea patients.

questions.prompt: A patient cannot tolerate nasal CPAP because of marked nasal obstruction. What alternative should be considered?
options: A full-face or oronasal CPAP interface
questions.answer: A full-face or oronasal CPAP interface
questions.rationale: An oronasal interface can allow treatment when nasal breathing is a major barrier to standard nasal CPAP.

questions.prompt: When titrating supplemental oxygen during a PAP study, oxygen is introduced and titrated upward by 1 L/min when the SpO2 remains below 88% for:
questions.rationale: Supplemental oxygen is typically introduced when SpO2 remains below 88% for 5 minutes during PAP titration.

questions.prompt: When oxygen is added during PAP because saturation remains low, what important principle still applies?
options: The technologist can ignore obstructive events
Underlying obstructive events still need appropriate PAP management
questions.answer: Underlying obstructive events still need appropriate PAP management
questions.rationale: Supplemental oxygen does not replace proper treatment of obstructive respiratory events.

questions.prompt: Which problem is supplemental oxygen most directly used to treat in sleep-lab respiratory thinking?
questions.rationale: Oxygen is used for oxygenation problems and may be part of care for hypoventilation or hypoxemia, not as a direct treatment for unrelated disorders.
